title: Weighted burst quotas and refund semantics for batched embeddings & rerank with external tool calls
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We currently overcharge customers in two common edge cases for non-chat pipelines (embeddings + rerank + external tool invocations / structured outputs):

1) Batched embeddings where some items succeed and others time out or fail: the billing pipeline often bills the entire batch unit to the customer even when results are not returned or are retried.
2) Rerank flows that call external tools (reranker -> tool) and the tool fails after the embedding calculation completes: tokens/embedding units are charged but downstream failure means customer did not get usable output; our product-level SLA expects better fairness.

Root cause hypothesis: billing is currently computed as a coarse aggregate at batch completion without atomic affinity to per-item success semantics, and refunds are manual post-facto reconciliations. Rate limiter buckets are also blind to endpoint family weights, so bursts from rerank pipelines can exhaust quotas intended for embeddings, creating unfair throttling under mixed workloads.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic, low-latency debit/refund model and a weighted burst quota policy so customers are charged only for successful, delivered work (or clearly-documented speculative prefetch) and quota exhaustion behavior is fair across embeddings, rerank, and tool families.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce per-item micro-charges for batched embeddings and rerank request trees. Each batch operation will emit a set of provisional charge events (debits) at the time of scheduling and a finalization event when item-level success/failure is known. Final charge = max(min_charge, calculated_units) for succeeded items; failed items emit a refund event that neutralizes the provisional debit.
- Implement idempotent debit/refund ledger operations keyed by request_id + item_index + billing_version to prevent double-charges on retries.
- Add "weighted burst" leaky-bucket per-customer: each endpoint family (embeddings, rerank, structured-tool) reserves a share of the burst allowance; when traffic concentrates in one family, weight-based throttling prevents starving other families.
- Update rate limiter to expose per-family remaining burst and overall bucket in API for console and alerts.
- Migration: run a reconciliation job for last 30 days to detect and auto-refund systemic overcharges where we can deterministically attribute failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit & integration tests demonstrating no double-charges for retries, correct refunds on partial-batch failures, and correct final ledger state in failure/success permutations.
- Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with realtime dashboards: charge inflight vs finalization rate, refund rates, and per-family burst utilization.
- No more than 0.1% increase in request tail-latency (95th) due to billing writes under typical load.
- Reconciliation job completes within SLO and issues refunds for >90% of deterministically-identifiable overcharges from the last 30 days.
notes: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after postmortem for INC-2026-03-07 (embeddings batch overcharge). Maya wrote initial problem statement.
2026-03-11: Architecture sync — agreed on provisional debit + finalization model. Tradeoff: additional writes to ledger vs billing correctness. Liam to prototype atomic debit/refund API.
2026-03-12: Spike done by Liam — prototype added idempotent ledger ops and per-item keys. Measured ~2ms additional latency on happy path; acceptable for P0.

2026-03-13: Design review with PM (Rohit Patel) and Finance (Elena Morales). Finance confirmed refund semantics and UX: refunds should appear as credits in console within billing cycle + email notification for refunds > $1000.

2026-03-14: Implementation started — created feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/7412. PR will contain ledger migration and rate-limiter changes. Planning canary for 2026-03-21.
Next steps: finish ledger API changes, add telemetry events, implement reconciliation job, add console panels for per-family burst visibility, and run canary.
Open question: how to label speculative prefetch vs user-visible work. Proposed: explicit header 'x-rw-speculation' that forces charge semantics to 'best-effort' (no refund). Need product decision.
migration_plan: 1) Roll out ledger API to canary; 2) Start writing provisional charges and finalization events (no refunds) in mirror-mode for 48h; 3) Enable refund path in canary; 4) Monitor refund ratios and latency; 5) Run 30-day deterministic reconciliation job and apply automated refunds where possible; 6) Full rollout after two successful canary windows.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for idempotent debit/refund semantics
- Integration tests for batched embeddings with permutations of success/failure/timeout
- Load test simulating mixed embeddings+rerank+tool traffic to validate burst fairness
- Canary metrics: (provisional_charges, finalized_charges, refunds, per_family_burst_util)
- Finance validation of billing statements in staging
implementation_notes:
- Billing event schema change: add fields billing_version (string), item_index (int as string), provisional_id (UUID string).
- Ledger writes must be idempotent and ordered by (request_id, item_index).
- Rate limiter: add family_weight config and per-customer burst windows.
- Console: expose per-family burst remaining and historical consumption charts.
